subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a framework-owned cron output target contract for file, channel, and session destinations, and which safety, fallback, and status semantics should be part of that public API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix adds public cron config/protocol surface and security-sensitive scheduled routing behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design unified output targets
options.body: Add a new cron output contract only after maintainers define path containment, recipient authorization, session injection, multi-target failure, and status accounting semantics.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella open but implement channel defaults, topic route selection, and no-channel failures through their narrower existing trackers first.

options.title: Decline framework routing
options.body: Keep output routing inside prompts/tools and document supported delivery modes, accepting the current model-compliance tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Design unified output targets
recommendation.body: Add a new cron output contract only after maintainers define path containment, recipient authorization, session injection, multi-target failure, and status accounting semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest recent-maintenance and policy-routing signal in the current checkout and prior ClawSweeper discussion for cron/config delivery surfaces.
